payload: Chandra X-ray Observatory on an Inertial Upper Stage: 50,162 lb (about 22,750 kg) with the stage and its support equipment, the heaviest payload launched on the Shuttle; 10,560 lb dry; crew of five
credit: Sources: NASA JSC STS-93 Space Shuttle Mission Report (all clock times, GMT), NASA STS-93 press kit (hardware figures), Chandra X-ray Center (current status). The stage's own firing times are given only as 'about one hour after' deployment in the report. Public domain / archive.

STS-93 Space Shuttle Mission Report (NASA JSC)

launch.source: NASA JSC STS-93 Space Shuttle Mission Report: orbit 144.7 by 153.7 nautical miles after the second orbital maneuvering burn, 153 by 163 after the separation burn. Launch from pad 39B

events.label: Launch — Columbia, Collins commanding
events.description: 23 July 1999 at 04:31 UTC (204:04:30:59.984 GMT, 12:31 a.m. EDT) from pad 39B, after scrubs on 20 July (hydrogen reading in the aft compartment) and 22 July (weather). Eileen Collins was the first woman to command a Shuttle mission.

events.label: Engine leak and electrical short at liftoff
events.description: About 5 s after engine start a loose pin in main engine 3 broke three hydrogen cooling tubes; the leak caused an early cutoff and a 16 ft/s underspeed. About 5 s after liftoff a half-second short on AC bus 1 disqualified two engine controllers. All three engines ran to cutoff.

events.label: Chandra and its upper stage deployed
events.description: Released at 204:11:47:01 GMT, MET 7 h 16 min, from the tilt table (raised to 29, then 58 degrees per the press kit). Columbia backed away 84 s later and fired the left main engine for 34 s at 12:02 GMT, ending in a 153 by 163 nautical mile orbit.

events.label: Upper stage fires twice
events.description: About one hour after release the first stage fired for two minutes; after a two-minute coast the second stage fired for two. The pair reached an orbit of 327 by 72,067 km. Chandra's own engine then fired five times to reach its working orbit.

events.label: Landing at Kennedy
events.description: Main gear touched down at 209:03:20:36 GMT, 27 July 1999, on runway 33 of the Shuttle Landing Facility after a deorbit burn at 02:19 GMT; wheels stopped at 03:21:22. Flight duration 4 d 22 h 49 min 36 s.
